# Bioconductor {.dark-slide background-color="#111C26"}

[BLOCK 3 &middot; PART B]{.eyebrow}

::: {.accent-bar}
:::

[Same repository format, released as versioned sets tied to R.]{.subhead}

## What Bioconductor is

A repository for genomic and high-throughput biological data analysis.
Bioconductor 3.23 has 2,418 software packages, plus annotation, experiment
data, workflow and book repositories
([release announcements](https://bioconductor.org/about/release-announcements/)).

It differs from CRAN in three ways:

- **Released as a set.** Twice a year.
- **Versioned.** Each release has its own repository URL, e.g.
  `bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/bioc`. CRAN has one repository that
  changes daily.
- **Tied to R.** Each Bioconductor release requires one R minor version.

## Each release requires one R version

```bash
curl -s https://bioconductor.org/config.yaml | grep -A1 'release_version'
```

```text
release_version: "3.23"
r_version_associated_with_release: "4.6.0"
```

The full mapping is `r_ver_for_bioc_ver` in the same
[config.yaml](https://bioconductor.org/config.yaml).

::: {.note}
[Planning]{.note-label}
The Bioconductor version your analyses need determines the R version you
install.
:::

## Two releases a year

| Release | Date | R |
|---|---|---|
| 3.23 | April 2026 | 4.6 |
| 3.22 | October 2025 | 4.5 |
| 3.21 | April 2025 | 4.5 |
| 3.20 | October 2024 | 4.4 |

Shortly before a new release, the previous one stops being built and its
branch is closed to commits
([release schedule](https://bioconductor.org/developers/release-schedule/)).
The old release stays downloadable; it just no longer changes.

## `BiocManager` picks the version

```r
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::version()
```

```text
[1] '3.23'
```

`BiocManager` derives the Bioconductor version from your R version. You do
not need to tell it
([`?BiocManager::version`](https://bioconductor.github.io/BiocManager/reference/version.html)).

```r
BiocManager::repositories()
```

```text
'getOption("repos")' replaces Bioconductor standard repositories, see
'help("repositories", package = "BiocManager")' for details.
Replacement repositories:
    CRAN: https://cloud.r-project.org
                                                BioCsoft 
           "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/bioc" 
                                                 BioCann 
"https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/data/annotation" 
                                                 BioCexp 
"https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/data/experiment" 
                                           BioCworkflows 
      "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/workflows" 
                                               BioCbooks 
          "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/books" 
                                                    CRAN

```

Five Bioconductor repositories **and CRAN**, because Bioconductor packages
depend on CRAN packages. The version number is in every URL.

## Bioconductor via `install.packages()`

Set the same vector yourself and `install.packages()` installs Bioconductor
packages:

```r
options(repos = BiocManager::repositories())
install.packages("BiocGenerics")
```

`BiocManager` takes CRAN from `getOption("repos")`, so a CRAN snapshot you
set there is used. It warns that `getOption("repos")` replaces its default
([`?BiocManager::repositories`](https://bioconductor.github.io/BiocManager/reference/repositories.html)).

::: {.note}
[Air-gapped sites]{.note-label}
An internal repository needs copies of the packages you use from each of
these URLs. We build one in block 6.
:::

## `BiocManager::install()` vs `install.packages()`

| | `install.packages()` | `BiocManager::install()` |
|---|---|---|
| Repositories | `getOption("repos")` | Bioconductor set for your R, plus CRAN |
| Checks R and Bioconductor match | No | Yes |
| Updates other packages | **No** | **Yes**, `update = TRUE` by default |
| Asks before updating | – | `ask = TRUE` by default |

```r
BiocManager::install("SummarizedExperiment")
```

That call installs one package **and offers to update every out-of-date
package in your library**, from Bioconductor and CRAN
([`?BiocManager::install`](https://bioconductor.github.io/BiocManager/reference/install.html)).


## `BiocManager::valid()`

```r
BiocManager::valid()
```

```text
'getOption("repos")' replaces Bioconductor standard repositories, see
'help("repositories", package = "BiocManager")' for details.
Replacement repositories:
    BioCsoft: https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/bioc
    BioCann: https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/data/annotation
    BioCexp: https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/data/experiment
    BioCworkflows: https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/workflows
    BioCbooks: https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/books
    CRAN: https://cloud.r-project.org
[1] TRUE
```

Checks that installed packages are neither out of date nor too new for your
R and Bioconductor versions
([`?BiocManager::valid`](https://bioconductor.github.io/BiocManager/reference/valid.html)).
Run it after changing a Bioconductor site library.

## Version mismatch

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

Exit the container and start one with an older R:

```bash
exit
docker run --rm -it rocker/r-ver:4.4.1 R -q
```

```r
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::version()
```

```text
[1] '3.20'
```

Same `BiocManager`, different answer. Now ask for a version that does not
match:

```r
BiocManager::install(version = "3.23")
```

```text
Error: Bioconductor version '3.23' requires R version '4.6'; use `version = '3.20'`
  with R version 4.4; see https://bioconductor.org/install
```

The error names the Bioconductor version this R can use.

::: {.note}
[Rule]{.note-label}
One Bioconductor version per library. Two Bioconductor versions need two
libraries. They share an R installation only if they use the same R minor
version, as the April and October releases of a year do (3.21 and 3.22 both
use R 4.5).
:::

```bash
exit      # back out; we start fresh in the next block
```
